title: El perro
goal: Deal with a dog that has decided your gate is its gate
culture: Street dogs here belong to the street rather than to nobody, and several houses feed the same one. Asking whose it is gets you a shrug: it is aquí anda — it is around. It is also almost certainly harmless.

beats.good: Ese perro, said with a nod at it. Whose it is turns out to be a harder question than you expect.

beats.es: No, no es mío. De nadie es.
beats.en: Not yours? Then whose is it?
ok: no es suyo y de quien es
beats.good: No es mío from her, no es suyo from you. The dog is fed by four houses and belongs to none of them, which is a normal arrangement.

beats.es: De nadie, pues. Aquí anda desde chiquito.
beats.good: Aquí anda — it is around. Andar is doing a great deal of work in this country and almost none of it is walking.

beats.es: No le haga caso. No muerde ese, es bien manso.
beats.objective: Check that — it does not bite?
beats.good: No muerde is the reassurance you will be given about every dog in Nicaragua, and it is nearly always true.
